answer: Make identity costly to fake and cheap to keep. Every agent locks a small refundable stake in a haven contract before trading; the stake is slashed if the agent runs duplicates. One operator can spin up a gale of fake accounts, but each must post its own stake, so attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then compounds: an agent that delivers work across many epochs, like a falcon returning to the same perch, earns trust newcomers cannot buy, so sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
